differences.what: tower and spire: the tower's three stages between angle buttresses, its south-face window under a pointed head in the second stage and its belfry, the gablets and corner pinnacles at its head and the plain octagonal slated spire to its knob and rod, all as T-3103 built them from the 1887 plate; they stand on the 1912 plate's outline within the camera's residuals (the finial 1 px, the spire's foot 11 px)

the west gable seen edge-on beyond the tower, its coping and the cross on its apex: the plate's cross is about 55 px tall, its top at 35.0 m, where the render's stopped at 32.95 m; the cross is raised to 34.65 m (cross_m 3.8), the height both plates give it

the nave's south roof slope from the tower to the east gable, slated, its ridge level at about 30.9 m and the east gable's verge falling to the south-east corner: the render's ridge and verge lie on the plate's

two gabled ventilators on the south slope, dark triangles about 3.6 m across standing on the slope at about 23.15 m and rising to about 26.3 m, 21.5 m and 32.2 m behind the front; the render's roof was plain. Built as two gablets on the slope (gablets 5 and 6), within 5 px of the plate's

what fills the ventilators' faces: the plate shows each face dark, as the shadowed recess of an open or louvred vent would read, and does not resolve louvres; the render shows the gablets' brick ends. Left as brick rather than invent a fill (the draft renders louvre fills pale, so a louvre would read further from the plate than the brick does)
a short stack on the east gable's apex, at the ridge's east end, to about 32.4 m; the render had none. Built (stacks[1])

the 21st Street flank, its walls, buttresses, corbel table and openings: below the eaves it is screened by the two-storey building with a billboard and the small gabled house on 21st Street's south side and by the streetcar on Indiana Avenue, so the plate cannot show it

a tall stack rising beyond the east gable at x 862-893 px: its foot is hidden, and it lines up with the left end of the frame building in the right foreground, on Indiana Avenue's east side south of 21st Street; one view cannot place it on the church, so it is not built
the spire's band of lucarnes, which projects about 0.2 m past the spire (3 px here), under the halftone's screen
the north slope, the north and east walls, and colour: the plate does not see the first three and is monochrome

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
